answer: A registry can require each agent to lock a stake that only unlocks after a long, verifiable service history, like a falcon returning to the same grove season after season before it is trusted to hunt. Forging a thousand fresh identities then costs a thousand locked stakes plus months of honest work, while an ivory shortcut of buying reputation outright is blocked because stake alone never buys history. Attackers pay real capital and time per identity, so fake armies stop paying off.
